newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks end down in mixed trade.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks end down in mixed trade.

text.p: The Australian share market closed narrowly weaker on Thursday, modest early gains whittled away by a falling September share price index contract which was chopped down by the local bond market.

The key share market barometer, the All Ordinaries index, slipped 1.1 points to close at 2,257.4. The September share price index dipped 12 points to 2,252 and was at a 5.4 point discount to the underlying index.
Brokers said futures were more sensitive than stocks to investor fears that U.S. financial markets could be hammered by economic data due to be released there later this week.
"I think the market would have finished a bit firmer if BHP had held its ground. BHP chased the SPI (futures) down and the SPI chased bonds down," a dealer from a Brisbane brokerage said.
Two key industrial issues underpinned the market on the day.
Transport group TNT rose following its better than expected year earnings report on Wednesday and paper company Amcor continued to recover on the back of a more positive earnings outlook.
Dealers said the resources sector was weighed down by majors BHP and CRA, despite buying interest in the gold, solid fuel and oil and gas sectors.
Dealers said the gold sector was supported by high turnover in Lihir Gold which rose 4.6 percent on the day.
Oil and gas issues were seen buoyed by the continuing conflict in the Gulf while the solid fuels sector was subject to a reweighting by the market on better outlook, dealers said.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about seven to six, while about 34 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
